content_units: You have   8 hours 30 minutes   total, so the most realistic plan is a   weakness-first review sprint   rather than full-course coverage. Priority should be:
Context used: all times are   Singapore Time (SGT)  , and the plan is designed for someone whose focus drops after about   90 minutes  .
Day   Dates   Focus   Key Sessions   Goal/Quiz

Day 1   2026-03-12 19:00-21:30   Networking basics   19:00-19:45 network models, ports, protocols; 19:45-19:55 break; 19:55-20:40 IP, DNS, DHCP, SOHO gear; 20:40-20:50 break; 20:50-21:30 recap + 10-15 mixed questions   Be able to explain common ports, IP basics, wireless standards, and router/switch/AP roles

Day 2   2026-03-13 06:30-08:00 and 19:30-22:00   Mobile devices + hardware troubleshooting   Morning: laptop parts, mobile accessories, ports, connectors; Evening block 1: printers, storage, display, boot/power faults; short break; block 2: troubleshooting method + symptom-to-cause drills; final recall quiz   Identify devices/cables quickly and choose first troubleshooting steps from symptoms

Day 3   2026-03-14 09:00-12:00   Networking reinforcement + cloud concepts + final mixed review   09:00-09:50 networking weak spots; 09:50-10:00 break; 10:00-10:45 cloud concepts + virtualization; 10:45-10:55 break; 10:55-11:40 hardware/mobile mixed questions; 11:40-12:00 final cheat-sheet recall   Leave with a compact memory sheet and confidence on the most missed topics
-   19:00-19:45  : OSI vs TCP/IP, LAN/WAN, bandwidth vs latency, common devices: router, switch, modem, access point.
-   19:45-19:55  : Break. Stand up, water, no phone scrolling.
-   19:55-20:40  : IPv4 basics, subnet idea at a high level, DNS, DHCP, NAT, common ports and protocols.
-   20:50-21:15  : Wireless standards, 2.4 GHz vs 5 GHz, WPA2/WPA3, common network troubleshooting scenarios.
-   21:15-21:30  : Active recall: write down 10 ports/protocols and 5 device roles from memory.
Day 2: Mobile Devices and Hardware Troubleshooting
-   06:30-07:10  : Mobile device types, laptop components, replacement parts, docking stations, screens, batteries.
-   07:20-08:00  : Ports/connectors and accessories: USB types, Lightning, USB-C, Thunderbolt, NFC, Bluetooth, biometrics.
-   19:30-20:15  : Hardware troubleshooting for power, boot, video, overheating, storage, memory.
-   20:25-21:05  : Printers and peripherals: laser vs inkjet, common printer failures, paper jams, faint prints, connectivity issues.
-   21:15-21:45  : Troubleshooting methodology: identify problem, theory, test theory, plan, verify, document.
-   21:45-22:00  : 10-12 mixed practice questions; review only missed items.
Day 3: Final Consolidation and Confidence Build
-   09:00-09:50  : Revisit networking misses only: ports, DHCP/DNS/NAT, Wi‑Fi, device roles.
-   10:00-10:45  : Cloud concepts: SaaS/PaaS/IaaS, public/private/hybrid cloud, shared resources, virtualization basics.
-   10:55-11:40  : Mixed timed set focused on mobile + hardware troubleshooting.
-   11:40-12:00  : Final brain dump sheet: ports, Wi‑Fi facts, connector chart, troubleshooting steps, cloud models.
- Memorize what is easy to score
- Do not start brand-new deep topics
Review Method That Fits This Time Limit
Use a   3-step loop   in every session:
- Focus on high-yield facts and exam-style distinctions.
- Write or say aloud: ports, acronyms, device roles, connector names, troubleshooting steps.
- Log misses in a short “last-day list”.
-   Networking basics  : flashcards and quick port/protocol drills
-   Hardware troubleshooting  : symptom → likely cause → first fix
-   Cloud concepts  : compare terms side by side
When tired, do   not   push into another heavy reading block. Switch to lighter, high-retention tasks:
- Review flashcards for   ports, protocols, connectors
- Do   5-question mini quizzes   instead of long sets
- Use   speak-from-memory recall   for troubleshooting steps
- Rewrite one-page summary sheets rather than reading chapters
If you must cut content, trim in this order:
3. Keep   networking basics   and   mobile connectors/components
4. Keep   troubleshooting methodology   no matter what
